original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Exact complete-call optimum of the unsigned five-source, all-31-binary-mask dirty connector over a ring of every characteristic c, with positive fixed tariffs; plus the run-walk optimum c(k + 2^k - 1) for k <= c sources.
scope_change_reason: Keep the unsigned alphabet and vary the coefficient characteristic. PR943 settles c = 2 and PR4225 settles c = 3; every other characteristic was open. This is a local interface classification, not supplier admission.
bottleneck_link: Shows that characteristic two is the only characteristic in which the five-source unsigned connector misses its per-operator floor, and that characteristic zero admits no restoring word. A physical consumer and complete costs remain missing before this can affect a recursive saving.
stop_rule: Stop after the characteristic classification, one explicit characteristic-four walk and bounded semantic verification. No further source-count census or family expansion.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json is regenerated byte for byte by verify.py. It holds the 108-call characteristic-3 and 144-call characteristic-4 words with readouts regenerated from all boundary multisets, and 41 run-walk cases for 2 <= c <= 9, k <= min(c, 7). Generic coefficient and dense dirty actions are checked, with eight semantic controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: For characteristic four and k = 6, 7, ... sources, where does the per-operator floor 4(k + 2^k - 1) first fail?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The run walk settles k <= c only. Characteristic four is the smallest case above three in which the source count can exceed the characteristic while the floor may still hold.
open_questions.first_step: Search length-4k walks for 4-fold prefix-sum coverage of all binary masks, starting at k = 6. Compare with the F3 n-source threshold question, which is a separate claim.

open_questions.question: Can a concrete consumer with characteristic c >= 3 coefficients use the 36c-call batch with a favorable full invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The abstract fixed-call optimum alone does not change a recursive supplier or kappa.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an immutable-source, unobserved-output caller over such a ring and price all 36 complete primitives, admission and dispatch.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical or selected-supplier consumer is instantiated in this package.
